claims.text: The target material is equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr in the cast state.
Adding 1 at.% Al to equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr will improve its oxygen resistance.
The 1 at.% Al addition will produce an alumina scale.
The alumina scale will be protective.
The protective alumina scale will prevent oxygen diffusion into the alloy.
The Al-modified alloy will exhibit a 30% lower oxidation rate than untreated equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr.
The predicted oxidation improvement applies at 800 °C.
The predicted oxidation improvement applies in air.
The predicted oxidation improvement applies over a 5 h exposure.
The predicted oxidation improvement applies without mechanical loading.
Adding 1 at.% Al will not compromise room-temperature mechanical performance.
Adding 1 at.% Al will not compromise high-temperature mechanical performance.
The magnitude of oxidation-rate reduction may depend on alloy composition and processing conditions.
The Al addition may affect the alloy's mechanical properties.
Oxidation resistance can be tested by exposing untreated and Al-modified samples to air at 800 °C for 5 h and measuring oxidation rate by thermogravimetry.
Failure of the Al-modified sample to reduce oxidation rate by at least 20% relative to the untreated sample is specified to falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis predicts that Al will not compromise mechanical performance, while the uncertainty field states that Al may affect mechanical properties and that this remains to be evaluated.

The prediction specifies a 30% oxidation-rate reduction, but the falsification rule only rejects reductions below 20%; a measured reduction from 20% to less than 30% would fail the stated quantitative prediction without falsifying it under the proposed rule.
